_doc: Intent -> concrete action/verb mapping used by the structured-intent DSL (reads/runs/write/dispatches). Users may edit this file to adjust boundaries. rules_dsl.py loads it when compiling rules; missing or malformed falls back to built-in defaults.
_read_actions_doc: Semantic actions classified as 'reads' after normalization (what the agent uses the read tool for).
_read_shell_verbs_doc: Shell verbs treated as 'read file content' (when the agent reads via a shell command, the run_command starts with or contains one of these).
_read_idioms_doc: Finer-grained 'definitely a read' idiom regexes (for python etc.): json.load(, .read(), open(single arg = read mode). When a command contains both one of these idioms and the target file, it is judged as a read. Note that open('x','w') (comma = write mode) does not match, so writes are not misclassified as reads.
_run_prefixes_doc: When matching 'runs', these prefix-word regexes are stripped from the subcommand head first (they are not the real program being invoked): timeout N, sudo, env, KEY=val, nice, exec, python -m, etc. After stripping, check whether the head is the target command.
_write_shell_ops_doc: Shell write redirects/commands: >, >>, tee, dd. never_writes recognises writes where one of these is followed by the target.
_write_idioms_doc: Definitely-write idioms (python etc.): open(...,'w'/'a'), .write(), json.dump(, .to_csv/.to_json. Writes done entirely inside a script (where the path does not appear in the command) still cannot be captured.
